name: ESL analog crossbar + KCL + ADC readout (parametric, domain-banded)
author: cp-4894 (WP-5, ADR-0005 D4) -- scales esl-crossbar-kcl (cp-4856) on esl-crossbar-array's \foreach generator (cp-4892, WP-4)
description: Parametric nrows x ncols VMM crossbar array (\foreach-generated, WP-4 pattern) whose per-column KCL summation node feeds a real circuitikz readout device -- resistor, capacitor, and current source across the three default columns, broadening circuitikz coverage beyond the to[R]/to[I] pair cp-4856 exercised, mixed with the hand-styled crossbar/KCL/vsource node vocabulary (the confirmed working pattern, ADR-0005 D4) -- and an ADC (contract §1a `adc`) producing a digital output word. The analog and digital regions are drawn as shaded domain-bands (`\domainband`) separated by a dashed domain-boundary (`\domainboundary`), the net-new region-shading convention opentikz had no equivalent of. Fixes the ported esl-crossbar-kcl fixture's known two-colliding-symbols defect (KCL node overlapping its readout device) via adequate \readoutgap/\adcgap clearance, verified by rendering to PNG.

parameters.name: \nrows
parameters.meaning: number of crossbar rows (VMM input rows)

parameters.name: \ncols
parameters.meaning: number of crossbar columns / readout-device columns

parameters.name: \readoutgap
parameters.meaning: clearance from a KCL node to its readout-device coordinate -- must stay large enough that the KCL node's circle does not visually overlap the readout device's circuitikz glyph (verify by rendering to PNG); this is the fix for the ported esl-crossbar-kcl fixture's known defect, which used 1.15cm

parameters.name: \adcgap
parameters.meaning: clearance from a readout device to its ADC triangle -- must stay large enough that the analog and digital domain-bands do not touch or overlap, leaving room for the dashed domain-boundary between them

edit_contract.node_naming: v-source: vin-<row> (generated, index-addressable); crossbar-cell: cell-<row>-<col> (generated, index-addressable); kcl-node: kcl-<col> (generated, index-addressable); adc: adc-<col> (generated, index-addressable); domain-band: (analogband); domain-band: (digitalband); domain-boundary: (bndL, bndR)

operations.summary:
edit 
rows/
cols -- the generator re-derives every node name, rail, KCL node, and readout column; the readout-device  oreach list (operations.change-readout-devices) must carry exactly 
cols entries afterward

edit the `\c/\dev/\devlabel in {...}` \foreach list's <device> tokens -- any real circuitikz bipole key (R, C, I, L, ...), NOT a figstyle node style; this is the one place this template mixes circuitikz bipoles with hand-styled tikzset nodes (cp-4856's confirmed working pattern)

if a readout device's circuitikz glyph is visually larger than the defaults tested (R/C/I), increase \readoutgap and/or \adcgap and re-render to PNG to confirm no symbol/node overlap before shipping -- do not shrink either below what the render confirms is collision-free

change the domain-semantic color for a whole role by re-binding that role's palette token (e.g. \colorlet{analogdomain}{...}); real circuitikz device glyphs (the readout devices, the ADC's outline) stay neutral/undyed -- only the hand-styled family nodes/wires and the domain-bands carry domain-semantic color

\domainband{name}{color-token}{fitspec}{label}{anchor} -- fitspec is normally an accumulated \xdef list built during the generator's \foreach loops (see \analogfitlist/\digitalfitlist), not a hand-typed node list; anchor should stay a "north ..." corner with the macro's inner sep=16pt (or larger) so the label never collides with the band's contents (verify by rendering to PNG)
\domainboundary{from}{to} between two named coordinates roughly midway between the two domain-bands -- draws the dashed divider contract §1a requires between two domains

invariants: a template must not name a semantic component the contract's §1 vocabulary does not define (§1 extensibility rule)
style/color bindings carry their contract §2 token role; a role's color is never swapped for decoration

substructure-recognition: recognize known analog SUBSTRUCTURES (current mirror, differential pair, cascode) as the placement UNIT and place them as a block, not transistor-by-transistor; the VMM crossbar-array is this family's concrete ESL substructure. Place blocks first, refine within.
symmetry-axis: matched/paired devices (a differential pair, mirrored current sources, a symmetric crossbar) are placed SYMMETRICALLY across a shared axis (usually vertical).
device-orientation: device ORIENTATION (rotation/flip) is part of placement, not just position — orient devices so pins face their connection and mirror matched devices about the symmetry axis.
power-ground-rails: the power/supply rail is PINNED at the top and the ground rail PINNED at the bottom; rails are placed/connected FIRST (VDD, GND net priority before signal nets).
signal-flow-direction: signal flows LEFT->RIGHT — primary inputs enter at the left, outputs exit at the right; place stages along that axis.
rows-are-inputs: crossbar-cell rows run HORIZONTAL; each row is one activation/input line driven from a v-source at the row's left end (rows left->right, row index increases downward).
cols-are-weights: crossbar-cell columns run VERTICAL; a column is a weight-cell stack sharing one bitline (column index increases left->right). Use crossbar-array for the grid.
current-sums-downward: per-column current flows DOWNWARD and accumulates; each column wire below cell (r,c) carries the running sum I_{1,c}+..+I_{r,c} (label it on the segment).
kcl-at-column-foot: each column terminates in exactly one kcl-node at the column FOOT (below the last cell), tagged "KCL"; the column current sums into it.
adc-below-kcl: the adc sits BELOW the kcl-node row (analog current in from the top apex-side, digital word out the far side); never above or beside the summation.
analog-digital-split: the analog/digital split is carried by a domain-band + one dashed domain-boundary; the digital region sits BELOW/AFTER the ADC, the analog accumulation above it.
body-font: Fonts match the chapter body — newtx Times text + math.
show-dont-tell: No equation/annotation callout boxes in the figure; equations live in \caption.
domain-labels-inside-bands: Domain labels sit INSIDE the shaded bands (small italic, top corner).
comma-subscripts: Two-index subscripts are comma-separated, row then column — G_{i,j}, I_{1,j}.
concrete-indices: Arrays use concrete indices (G_{2,2}), no generic highlighted exemplar cell.

typed-wires: Wire color encodes domain — orange=analog current (awire), gray=digital word (dwire), blue=input voltage (vwire) — the token->role binding is reserved and never swapped across the analog/digital or voltage/current domain boundary (e.g. awire never carries a v-source-to-cell edge, vwire never carries a cell-to-KCL edge). Stealth arrowheads everywhere.

circuitikz-bipole-reservation: circuitikz `to[...]` bipoles are reserved for real EE devices (resistor, current/voltage source, capacitor, etc.); crossbar cells, KCL nodes, and voltage-source glyphs stay the hand-styled figstyle-derived node styles (cell/kclnode/vsource) — never redraw a cell as a circuitikz bipole, and never redraw a real device as a plain hand-styled node. Mixing the two idioms in one figure is intentional and must stay legible (label each readout branch).
kcl-current-label-clearance: every KCL node has a labeled incoming-current annotation (currentlbl) placed clear of neighboring columns.

palette-additive-not-remapped: the ESL domain-semantic tokens (inputdomain/weightdomain/digitaldomain/ analogdomain) are ADDITIVE to opentikz's five ot* names — never remapped onto or aliased through otblue/otorange/otteal/otpurple/otgray.
kcl-not-sigma-glyph: Column sum is a KCL node (joined lines + a small "KCL" tag), not a bare Sigma.
xw-is-digital-logic: x_i . w_{i,j} is a digital multiply (XNOR for +-1, AND for 0/1); the product gates a per-cell current source labeled DAC — signal is analog ONLY after the DAC.
running-column-sums: Column wires carry running sums — below (1,1) is I_{1,1}; below (2,1) is I_{1,1}+I_{2,1}; the KCL yields I_j.
adcbuffer-is-zoomin: adcbuffer is the zoom-in of the Sigma+ADC stage of mixed-signal-mac; keep aligned.
